doc.calendar: the calendar the export comes from (below) — information only; by its "id" the import recognises a document from another calendar
doc.range: the days the export covered (below) — information only; the import looks for appointments with "id" in them
doc.schemes: the appointment schemes of this calendar for reference (below) — which "values" the appointments may have; the import doesn’t change them (schemes are changed in “Appointment schemes”)

schemes.name: scheme name — for an appointment’s "scheme" (when unambiguous)
schemes.kind: the kind of appointments of this scheme
schemes.kinds: the kinds to choose from for an appointment of this scheme
schemes.fields: the scheme’s fields — the keys of an appointment’s "values" ("level": "day" — keys of a day’s "values" in "occurrences"); the field is described below

appointment.id: appointment id from an export — the appointment will be changed; without "id" — a new appointment
appointment.key: a short name (letters, digits, - and _) for "@key" references in this document ("parent")
appointment.remove: true — remove this appointment (the whole series, together with its program points); only with "id"; an appointment with accepted intentions, entries or bookings stays (the import says so)
appointment.kind: kind: {kinds}; missing for a new one: the kind of the scheme or the calendar
appointment.title: title (up to {max} characters); required for a new appointment — except a mass, confession and devotion: their name is public (mass plan, notice board), and without it only the kind is shown (“Mass”)
appointment.start: start: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", or "YYYY-MM-DD" — all day; in a program point also "HH:MM" (on the day of the parent appointment); a new point without "start" begins with the parent appointment
appointment.end: end: "HH:MM" (the same day) or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"; for all day the last day "YYYY-MM-DD"; missing: a new one lasts as long as the calendar says (all day — one day), a changed one keeps its length; at most 14 days (all day: 60 days)
appointment.allDay: true — all day (a "start" without a time does the same)
appointment.link: “More information”: "https://…" or "#/address" of a page on recreatio.pl
appointment.linkLabel: text on the link button (up to {max} characters)
appointment.weekdays: with "weekly": days {days} (or numbers 1–7, 1 = Monday); missing: the day of "start"
appointment.until: last day of the series "YYYY-MM-DD"; null — no end; missing for a new series: no end
appointment.bookable: true / false — whether this appointment can be booked (only in a calendar with bookings); null — as the calendar
appointment.capacity: places for this appointment (1–{max}); null — as the calendar
appointment.scheme: the appointment’s scheme: "name" or "id" from "schemes"; null — universal (an export of a calendar with schemes writes null for appointments without a scheme); missing for a new appointment: the scheme of its kind if the calendar has exactly one, otherwise universal; a new program point — universal
appointment.values: values of the scheme fields of the whole appointment: {"field key": "text"}; "" or null clears the field; missing — unchanged
appointment.occurrences: chosen days of the series (below): cancelled, moved, with values of day fields
appointment.points: program points: appointments under this appointment, in this order — with the same keys
appointment.parent: the parent appointment of an appointment in "appointments": the "@key" of an appointment in this document or the "id" of an appointment outside it; null — detach from the program; missing — unchanged

occurrence.date: day of the series "YYYY-MM-DD" — the one it falls on according to the series (also when it is moved); required
occurrence.cancelled: true — cancel this day (a mass with accepted intentions or an appointment with entries stays — the import says so); false — return it to the series (neither cancelled nor moved)
occurrence.start: move this day: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" or "HH:MM" (that day); the length stays
occurrence.values: values of the scheme fields of this day ("level": "day"): {"field key": "text"}; "" or null clears the field; missing — unchanged

samples.masses: masses with a scheme and series days

occurrence.title: Series day ("occurrences[]")
occurrence.lead: A chosen day of an appointment — usually of a series. A day is named by its date: the day it falls on according to the series, also when it is moved. Days without an entry stay as they are.
occurrence.tail: The export lists the days of the range that are cancelled, moved or have values. An appointment that doesn’t repeat has one day — the day of its "start".

appointment.title: Appointment ("appointments[]", "points[]")
appointment.lead: An appointment has the same keys as the appointments of a page and an area ("title", "start", "end", "location", "points", "repeat" …) — plus "id", "kind", "scheme", "values" and "occurrences". For a changed appointment, a key that is missing stays unchanged.
appointment.retime: Changing the time of a series ("start", "end", "repeat", "every", "weekdays", "until", "count") changes all its days — including past ones. Cancelled and moved days not in "occurrences" then return to the series; those in "occurrences" the import writes again. Intentions and entries follow the day; when the day no longer exists, the appointment stays unchanged (the import says so). “Different from this day on” (“this and following”) is done in the appointment editor.
appointment.values: Values ("values"): "choice" and "colour" — a value or a name from the field’s list; "number" — a number; "bool" — "tak" (yes) or "nie" (no) (also true / false); "date" — "YYYY-MM-DD"; "time" — "HH:MM"; "link" — https://… or #/…; "person" — a role id. Public fields up to {max} characters. A required field ("required") must have a value — otherwise a new appointment is skipped and changes to an existing one are not saved.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- The appointments are seen by everyone who has the key of the area that sees the calendar (“Who sees” in the calendar settings) — also through an access link; when that area is public (“everyone reads”), by everyone, also without an account.
- Calendar (Day, Week, Month, List): program points stand in the grid next to their appointment; the appointment details show the place, note, link, scheme values and the day’s entry lists (intentions, sign-ups). “Now”: “Upcoming appointments” (today and tomorrow), and in “Waiting for you” — “Appointments today”.
- Page modules: “Calendar” (chosen calendars), “Event program” (an appointment with points — "points"), “Booking” (appointments to choose from); an appointment set as the area’s main appointment — in the modules “Events” and “Business card”, when everyone sees it. On a page everyone sees what they can open; a module of a public page can also be embedded as a widget on another website.
- Masses, confessions and devotions ("kind") are also in “Masses and services” (parish office). When the area that sees the calendar is public, their names and times (for a mass also the public scheme fields) go to the public plan — the page module “Masses and services” — and masses also to the notice-board printout; the place and notes are not there.
- "bookable" and "capacity" (a calendar with bookings): the appointment can be chosen in the module “Booking”; in the Calendar it shows the number of taken places, and requests wait in “To confirm”.
- Appointments have no reminders (tasks do), and the import notifies no one.

calendar.title: Calendar appointments ("{format}")
calendar.lead:
The appointments of ONE calendar: single and repeating (series — e.g. a weekly lesson plan or weekday masses), all-day, with a place, note and link, with a program (points under an appointment), with the calendar’s scheme and its values, and with chosen days of a series (cancelled, moved, with their own values). Masses, confessions and devotions are appointments here like any other ("kind").
Export (calendar settings → “Appointments as JSON”; whoever only sees the calendar: “Calendars” → “Export JSON”): the appointments of the chosen range (by default from today for a year) and the series that reach into it — each with "id".
The import changes IN PLACE: an appointment with "id" (from an export of this calendar) is changed, an appointment without "id" is added. A key that is missing stays unchanged — "id" and what changes are enough; "" or null clears a text. Nothing disappears unless the appointment has "remove": true. Before the import you see the list of changes and the warnings; the same document imported a second time changes nothing.
Titles, places, notes, links and non-public values are encrypted in the browser with the key of the area that sees the calendar — just as in the appointment editor. The export file holds them in plain text: it is your copy.
The import does not change: mass intentions (a separate format for masses and intentions), list entries (sign-ups), bookings, people at an appointment, or who sees an appointment (the calendar says that).
A document from another calendar ("calendar" with another "id") is a copy: its appointments will be added as new ones.
calendar.time: Time is local (the calendar’s time zone), without a zone: a moment "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", a day "YYYY-MM-DD", a time "HH:MM".
calendar.limits: Limits: {entries} appointments including points in one document, a program up to {depth} levels, {days} days per appointment in "occurrences".
